summary.headline: Kiri Industries Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs.241 crore, but reported EBITDA was hit by Rs.114 crore of non-cash year-end adjustments.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 29% YoY to Rs.241 crore, with management citing volume recovery, better dye intermediate realisations and lower legal costs. Management said adjusted EBITDA was about Rs.35 crore, but Rs.114 crore of non-cash closing-period mark-to-market adjustments were booked, which weighed on reported EBITDA. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% to Rs.251 crore and finance cost fell to Rs.8 crore from Rs.54 crore a year earlier. The DyStar award was monetised in FY26 and the copper and fertiliser project (Indo Asia Copper) moved into engineering, ordering and civil works, with commercial operations guided from April 2027 to March 2029.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone adjusted EBITDA (Q4 FY26, post year-end adjustments)

financial_highlights.value: Rs.79 crore (~10% margin); Rs.69 crore cited later in call

financial_highlights.value: Rs.188 crore (Rs.58 crore Lonsen Kiri, Rs.129 crore DyStar up to Q2 FY26)

segments.name: Dyes and Dyes Intermediates (standalone)
segments.commentary: Dyes Intermediates contributed 52% of revenue, Dyes 33% and Basic Chemicals 15%. Management targets over Rs.1,000 crore standalone revenue in FY27, about 20% growth.

segments.name: Lonsen Kiri JV (40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs.58 crore to FY26 share of profit. Management said the JV generated about Rs.1,100 crore of sales and expects it to cross Rs.1,300 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Indo Asia Copper / copper and fertiliser project
segments.commentary: Pre-operative; FY26 costs were capitalised and management said it is EBITDA and PAT neutral. No copper revenue is expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Standalone EBITDA margin target of 10% to 15%; management said 12% for the current year would be satisfactory.
Dyes standalone revenue target above Rs.1,000 crore in FY27 (about 20% growth); JV revenue expected above Rs.1,300 crore.

Copper and fertiliser project: commercial operations to start unit by unit from April 2027, with full operation by March 2029. Earlier guidance of Rs.20,000-25,000 crore revenue was reframed as roughly Rs.40,000 crore-plus across the project at current pricing.
Capex: about Rs.4,500-5,000 crore by March 2027, another about Rs.5,000 crore in FY28, and Rs.2,000-3,000 crore by March 2029, totalling about Rs.13,000 crore including interest during moratorium.

Debt: minimal debt in FY27 (under Rs.1,000 crore); capex debt of about Rs.4,000-5,000 crore and working capital of Rs.3,000-5,000 crore in FY28, taking total debt to Rs.8,000-9,000 crore. Expected interest rate 8.5-9%, with a three-year principal moratorium.
Government incentives of about 30-35% of eligible capex over 10 years, or roughly Rs.3,000-3,500 crore a year, are in final approval stage.
Fertiliser trading under Indo Asia Fertilizer to begin from next quarter of FY27; copper trading not yet started.
No dividend for FY26 and none to be declared this year; buyback undecided.
capex_capacity: Copper rod, tube and refinery engineering under Tata Consulting Engineers; key machinery and utility packages ordered; long-lead equipment ordering ongoing.
Utilities work under way including oxygen facility and sulfuric acid plant; desalination, renewable integration and logistics facilities in planning.
Civil construction across the site about 25-30% complete. About Rs.2,500 crore already spent or committed in advances, machinery and similar.

Copper concentrate requirement for the primary line is about 1.5 million tonnes; more than 1 million tonnes is under non-binding tie-ups, with the balance targeted by next year. Rock phosphate is said to be 100% tied up.
Financial closure not yet done but said to be near; disclosure expected within a few months.
demand_pricing: Management sees China's tightening of key dye intermediates from environmental compliance and production curbs as supportive of Indian producers' realisations.
Textile customers (over 95% of dyes and chemicals customers) are extending payments, which lengthens Kiri's payables; average payable cycle quoted as 90-120 days.
Management said copper will remain import-dependent until 2030-2035 despite domestic capacity additions, with EV and AI data-centre demand rising.
Secondary copper capacity additions in India are linked to global availability of ingots and blister as exporting countries ban concentrate exports; scrap supply is also rising domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Is the April 2027 phase-one start and Rs.20,000-25,000 crore revenue outlook still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations start unit by unit from FY27-28, with Rs.40,000 crore-plus revenue cited for the project at current pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.160 crore tax provision and net DyStar proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.150 crore has been paid, on the view that most of the award is a judicial capital receipt rather than taxable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Rs.114 crore adjustment booked and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it relates to mark-to-market on temporary parking of surplus funds in debt, equity and hybrid instruments within India, and it will not recur every quarter or year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest rate and moratorium on the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected rate 8.5-9%, with principal repayment starting three years after drawdown and interest serviced from day one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pay dividends or buybacks?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend this year and none to be declared; buyback has not been decided and cash is being retained to fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the backup if plant utilisation is low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt servicing requires about 50% utilisation; below that it would be a problem, while sales are not seen as a constraint.

risks_watch: Non-cash mark-to-market adjustments of Rs.114 crore in Q4 depressed reported EBITDA; the company says they are non-recurring, but reported and adjusted figures diverge materially.
Copper concentrate tie-up is only non-binding for over 1 million tonnes against a 1.5 million tonne requirement; the balance is still open.
Debt build-up to Rs.8,000-9,000 crore in FY28 at 8.5-9% interest; servicing depends on about 50% plant utilisation, per management.
Tax treatment of the DyStar award (Rs.150 crore paid) rests on an expert legal opinion.
Receivables from textile customers are stretching and pushing out payables, which raises working capital needs.
Financial closure is still pending and the incentive approvals are awaited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the copper and fertiliser project timeline and on dyes recovery, but defensive and repetitive when asked about the Q4 EBITDA swing, the Rs.114 crore adjustment and shareholder returns. Management declined to commit on buybacks and gave no firm date on financial closure.
key_quotes: So, the EBITDA for the year ended is 79 crores on a standalone basis and 127 crores on the consolidated basis.
And if it doesn't happen, even if the plant operations remain below 50%, still we would be able to service the interest and service the debt.
But this year, the dividend has not been declared and is not going to be declared.
